title: Reaction-diffusion systems, invariants and pattern computation

items.title: Reaction vector fields and quasi-positivity

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §0, printed p. 1: concentrations of several species and a coupled reaction vector; §4, printed pp. 26–27: the boundary sign criterion for positivity of a locally Lipschitz semidiscrete ODE.

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.6–10.7, PDF pp. 149–151: scalar and vector reaction-diffusion formulations and the Jacobian linearization at a homogeneous equilibrium.

items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be locally Lipschitz. Write $F_i$ for its $i$th component. The autonomous reaction equation is $z'(t)=F(z(t))$. The field is **quasi-positive** on $U\cap[0,\infty)^m$ if, for every $i$ and every $z\in U\cap[0,\infty)^m$ with $z_i=0$, one has $F_i(z)\ge0$. This condition concerns only the coordinate faces of the nonnegative orthant.

For a rectangle $R=\prod_{i=1}^m[a_i,b_i]\subset U$ with $a_i<b_i$, the field is **inward-pointing on $R$** if $F_i(z)\ge0$ whenever $z\in R$ and $z_i=a_i$, and $F_i(z)\le0$ whenever $z\in R$ and $z_i=b_i$. If $a_i=0$ for every $i$, quasi-positivity supplies the lower-face half of this condition, but the upper-face inequalities remain separate hypotheses. Neither boundary condition by itself asserts that a numerical update preserves $R$.

For smoothness-dependent results below, $F\in C^4(U,\mathbb R^m)$ will be stated explicitly. No smoothness beyond local Lipschitz continuity is built into this definition.

items.title: Periodic rectangular reaction-diffusion grid

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.6–10.8, printed pp. 144–148 (PDF pp. 149–153): multispecies reaction-diffusion equations, two-species linear stability and Turing context, and the FitzHugh–Nagumo illustration with a periodic centered-difference Laplacian (Listing 10.1).

items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, side lengths $L_j>0$, and integers $N_j\ge3$. Put $h_j=L_j/N_j$, $\mathbb T_L^d=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$, and $G_h=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb Z/N_j\mathbb Z)$. Grid nodes are $x_i=((i_j+\tfrac12)h_j)_{j=1}^d$ modulo the side lengths, grid indices wrap modulo $N_j$, and $P_hu=(u(x_i))_{i\in G_h}$ denotes sampling. The cell volume is $m_h=\prod_jh_j$. The positive periodic heat stencil is the unit-diffusivity specialization of the periodic operator in [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]]:
$$
(A_h^{\rm per}v)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\frac{2v_i-v_{i+e_j}-v_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.
$$
For $s$ species with diffusivities $d_r\ge0$, the reaction-diffusion grid generator acts on species $r$ by $-d_rA_h^{\rm per}$. Each grid node has weight $m_h=\prod_jh_j$; the stencil has zero row and column sums, so each species' weighted sum is conserved by diffusion. Its matrix representation satisfies $L_h=m_hA_h^{\rm per}$, with symmetric $L_h$, nonpositive off-diagonal entries and $L_h\mathbf1=0$.

The sign convention is that $A_h^{\rm per}$ is nonnegative and $-d_rA_h^{\rm per}$ generates diffusion. The exact eigenvalues of the positive stencil are supplied by [[lem-periodic-heat-difference-amplification-symbol]]. This grid is the only spatial discretization used in the periodic error theorem; no mesh-uniform claim for general finite-volume meshes is made there.

items.title: Inward reaction rectangles

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 26–27: inward signs on the boundary of the nonnegative orthant for a positive ODE flow. A bounded rectangle additionally requires upper-face signs, stated here.

items.statement:
Let $F:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be locally Lipschitz, and let $R=\prod_{i=1}^m[a_i,b_i]\subset U$ with finite $a_i<b_i$. The rectangle is **reaction-inward** if, for every $i$, $F_i(z)\ge0$ on the lower face $z_i=a_i$ and $F_i(z)\le0$ on the upper face $z_i=b_i$, with all other coordinates in their intervals. It is **reaction-invariant** if the solution map $\Phi_F^t$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ on $R$ and $\Phi_F^t(R)\subseteq R$ for every $t\ge0$.

For a rectangle with $a_i=0$ for all $i$, the lower-face condition is exactly quasi-positivity from [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]]. The upper-face condition is independent and must be checked separately. The inward-sign condition is a hypothesis, not by definition an invariance theorem.

items.title: Stoichiometric conservation and dissipation functionals

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §0, printed p. 1: mass conservation as a qualitative requirement for transport-reaction discretizations. The weighted linear-functional convention here is defined explicitly.

items.statement:
Let $F:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be the reaction vector field of [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]], and let $R\subset U$ be a state set. A vector $c\in[0,\infty)^m$ is a **stoichiometric conservation vector on $R$** if $c^TF(z)=0$ for every $z\in R$. It is a **stoichiometric dissipation vector on $R$** if $c^TF(z)\le0$ for every $z\in R$. The corresponding pointwise mass is $c^Tz$.

For a measurable domain $\Omega$, the continuous total mass is $\mathcal M_c(u)=\int_\Omega c^Tu(x)\,dx$. For any finite index set $I$ with assigned positive weights $m_i$, the discrete total mass of states $U_i\in\mathbb R^m$ is $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U)=\sum_{i\in I}m_ic^TU_i$. The weights and index set are part of the discrete model. Conservation and dissipation always refer to these stated functionals and the stated state set; no claim is made for a different weight vector or for reactions outside $R$.

items.title: Semilinear vector reaction-diffusion systems

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §0, printed p. 1: the vector concentration equation for several species with diffusion and local reaction terms; §9, printed pp. 60–64: splitting the evolution into reaction and diffusion subproblems.

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.6–10.7, PDF pp. 149–151: the vector reaction-diffusion equation and linearization at a homogeneous equilibrium.

items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)$ with $d_i\ge0$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be as in [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]]. A **semilinear vector reaction-diffusion system** is
$$
u_t=D\Delta u+F(u),\qquad u(x,0)=u_0(x),
$$
on either a flat periodic torus $\mathbb T_L^d$ or a bounded connected polyhedral domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with homogeneous no-flux conditions $\partial_nu_i=0$ for every component. The diffusion matrix is diagonal and independent of $u$; this definition does not include cross-diffusion.

A classical solution is **bounded in the rectangle $R$** on $[0,T]$ if $u(x,t)\in R$ at every point and time in its stated solution class, with $R$ as in [[def-reaction-invariant-rectangle]]. This item fixes the continuous PDE convention; the finite-volume and periodic discrete operators are defined separately.

items.title: No-flux TPFA diffusion generator

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, updated author text, 2019
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2, PDF pp. 38–44: interior-face transmissibilities and shared conservative TPFA fluxes.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: §2, PDF pp. 8–10: orthogonal TPFA fluxes, positive transmissibilities, and the weighted stiffness matrix.

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal T=(\mathcal K,\mathcal F)$ be a finite TPFA-admissible cell-face mesh from [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]] and [[def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme]]. Impose homogeneous no-flux boundary conditions: boundary faces contribute zero flux and therefore no conductance. For adjacent cells $K,L$, set
$$
c_{KL}=\sum_{F=K|L}T_F,
$$
where the sum is over their common interior faces and is zero when they are not adjacent. Set $c_{KL}=c_{LK}$ and $m_K=|K|$. If more than one face separates a cell pair, summing their conductances gives the same cell-balance flux as retaining the faces separately. Define the symmetric matrix $L_h$ by $(L_h)_{KK}=\sum_{L\ne K}c_{KL}$ and $(L_h)_{KL}=-c_{KL}$ for $K\ne L$.

For species diffusivities $d_r\ge0$, the no-flux finite-volume diffusion equation is $M U_r'+d_r L_h U_r=0$ for each species $r$, where $M=\operatorname{diag}(|K|)$. Its component equation is
$$
|K|(U_{K,r})'=d_r\sum_{L:c_{KL}>0}c_{KL}(U_{L,r}-U_{K,r}).
$$
The equality is the usual shared-face TPFA balance with outward flux $T_F(U_{K,r}-U_{L,r})$ and no boundary flux. The matrix $L_h$ is symmetric, has zero row sums and nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and obeys $v^{\mathsf T}L_hv=\sum_{\{K,L\}}c_{KL}(v_K-v_L)^2\ge0$, where the sum is over unordered adjacent cell pairs. With $M=\operatorname{diag}(|K|)$, the generator $-M^{-1}L_h$ is self-adjoint in the weighted pairing $\langle v,w\rangle_M=v^{\mathsf T}Mw$. This definition makes no accuracy claim for arbitrary admissible meshes.

items.title: Inward reaction fields preserve rectangles and stoichiometric mass

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 26–27: inward boundary signs for positive semidiscrete reaction ODEs; the local proof supplies the full rectangle argument.

items.statement: Let $R=\prod_{i=1}^m[a_i,b_i]$ be the reaction-inward rectangle of [[def-reaction-invariant-rectangle]]. Assume $F$ from [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]] is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of $R$, and its derivative is bounded on some closed neighborhood of $R$. For any $z_0\in R$, the IVP $z'=F(z)$ has a unique solution for every $t\ge0$, and $z(t)\in R$. If $c$ is a conservation vector on $R$, then $c^Tz(t)=c^Tz_0$; if it is a dissipation vector, then $c^Tz(t)$ is nonincreasing. The lower-face condition is quasi-positivity when $a_i=0$; upper-face inwardness remains a separate hypothesis.

items.title: A bounded forward-Euler reaction step preserves an inward rectangle

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §6, printed pp. 39–40: forward-Euler positivity under an explicit reaction Lipschitz step bound; the local proof gives the rectangle and mass version.

items.statement:
Let $R=\prod_{i=1}^m[a_i,b_i]$ be reaction-inward for $F$ from [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]]. Assume for each $i$ there is a coordinate Lipschitz constant $L_i\ge0$ such that $|F_i(z)-F_i(w)|\le L_i|z_i-w_i|$ whenever $z,w\in R$ differ only in coordinate $i$. Define
$$
\tau_R=\min_{i:L_i>0}L_i^{-1},
$$
with $\tau_R=+\infty$ if every $L_i=0$. For $z\in R$ and $0\le\tau\le\tau_R$, the forward-Euler reaction step $z^+=z+\tau F(z)$ lies in $R$. For every conservation vector $c$ on $R$, $c^Tz^+=c^Tz$; for every dissipation vector, $c^Tz^+\le c^Tz$.

items.title: Cell-centered rectangular TPFA grid with homogeneous no-flux boundaries

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, updated author text, 2019
references.locator: Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3, PDF pp. 38–47: orthogonal cell-centered TPFA fluxes and boundary-face conventions.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d(0,L_j)$, where $L_j>0$, and let integers $N_j\ge2$ define $h_j=L_j/N_j$. The finite cell set is $I_h=\prod_{j=1}^d\{0,\ldots,N_j-1\}$, cell centers are $x_i=((i_j+\tfrac12)h_j)_{j=1}^d$, and every cell has volume $m_h=\prod_jh_j$. This is the uniform orthogonal Cartesian mesh; adjacent center segments are perpendicular to their shared faces. Take the scalar cellwise coefficient to be $\lambda_K=1$ and give boundary faces homogeneous no-flux data, so they contribute no flux.

For a grid vector $v=(v_i)_{i\in I_h}$, define the positive cell-centered stencil
$$
(A_h^Nv)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\frac{2v_i-v_{i+e_j}-v_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2},
$$
where an unavailable neighbor at a boundary is assigned the value of the boundary cell itself. Indeed a face normal to direction $j$ has area $|F|=m_h/h_j$ and adjacent centers are distance $h_j$ apart, so its TPFA transmissibility is $|F|/h_j=m_h/h_j^2$; dividing the cell balance by $m_h$ gives the displayed coefficient. Boundary faces contribute zero flux. Thus $M_h=m_hI$ and $L_h^N=m_hA_h^N$ are the mass and stiffness matrices of the no-flux specialization in [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]]. For species diffusivities $d_r\ge0$, the finite-volume diffusion equation is $U_r'=-d_rA_h^NU_r$.

Define the doubled periodic grid with $2N_j$ cells per direction on side lengths $2L_j$, using the same widths $h_j$, as in [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]. The reflection map $E_h$ extends $U$ evenly across every boundary face: in one coordinate, its extended index is $i$ for $0\le i<N_j$ and $2N_j-1-i$ for $N_j\le i<2N_j$; apply this coordinatewise. This finite reflection convention is used in the error theorem below.

items.title: Continuous reaction-diffusion mass balance on boxes, tori, and piecewise C1 domains

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §0, printed p. 1: mass-balance modeling for multiple species; the local proof supplies the continuous no-flux and periodic identities.

items.statement:
Let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^m))$ solve $u_t=D\Delta u+F(u)$, with constant diagonal $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)$, and let its range lie in $R$. Let $c$ be a conservation or dissipation vector on $R$. One may take (i) a box $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d[0,L_j]$ with periodic identification or homogeneous Neumann data, or (ii) a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentation as in [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]], assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in this second branch and homogeneous Neumann data on every face outside the edge set. For either branch,
$$
\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega c^Tu(x,t)\,dx=\int_\Omega c^TF(u(x,t))\,dx.
$$
Hence the total mass is constant when $c^TF=0$ on $R$ and nonincreasing when $c^TF\le0$ on $R$. The first branch is choice-free; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used only for the stated piecewise $C^1$ divergence-theorem branch.

items.title: Second-order spatial consistency of the periodic FV heat stencil

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 28–29: centered diffusion stencils and their second-order spatial truncation error.

items.statement:
Let $u_r\in C^4(\mathbb T_L^d)$, and let $P_hu_r$ denote its samples on the periodic rectangular grid of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]. For every grid node $i$,
$$
\left|(A_h^{\rm per}P_hu_r)_i+P_h(\Delta u_r)_i\right|\le\frac1{12}\sum_{j=1}^dh_j^2\|\partial_{jjjj}u_r\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d)}.
$$
For $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)$, define the sampled spatial residual $r_h=D(P_h\Delta u-\Delta_hP_hu)$, where $\Delta_h=-A_h^{\rm per}$ acts componentwise. If the indicated fourth derivatives are uniformly bounded for $0\le t\le T$, then $\|r_h(t)\|_\infty\le C_{\rm sp}h_{\max}^2$ with $C_{\rm sp}=\frac{d_{\max}}{12}\sum_j\|\partial_{jjjj}u\|_{L^\infty}$ componentwise, uniformly in the mesh.

items.title: Mesh-uniform reaction-diffusion commutator bound on a periodic grid

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §9, printed pp. 60–61: the Lie local defect contains the commutator; the notes explicitly warn that mesh-uniform bounds require control of the commutator terms.

items.statement:
Let $u:[0,T]\times\mathbb T_L^d\to R$ have bounded spatial derivatives through order two, with $R$ a compact rectangle. Let $F\in C^2$ on a neighborhood of $R$, and let $\mathcal A_h=-D A_h^{\rm per}$ be the periodic-grid diffusion generator from [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]. Define $F_h(P_hu)=P_h(F(u))$ pointwise. Then, uniformly over all periodic grids with $h_j=L_j/N_j$ and $N_j\ge3$,
$$\sup_{\substack{N_j\ge3\ (1\le j\le d),\ 0\le t\le T}}\left\|\mathcal A_hF_h(P_hu(t))-DF(P_hu(t))\mathcal A_hP_hu(t)\right\|_\infty\le C_{\rm com}<\infty,$$
where $C_{\rm com}$ depends only on the dimension, $D$, the suprema of $D^2u$, $DF$, $D^2F$, and the compact state rectangle, not on the mesh widths. This is the finite-grid commutator used in the first-order split-error proof; it is not a claim for arbitrary meshes or unbounded operators.

items.title: Two-species continuous and discrete dispersion criteria

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.7–10.8, PDF pp. 150–153: two-species diffusion-dependent mode matrices and the reaction-diffusion model example.

items.statement:
Let $F\in C^1$ and let $y_*\in\mathbb R^2$ be a homogeneous equilibrium, $F(y_*)=0$. Set $J=DF(y_*)=(J_{ij})$, assume $\operatorname{tr}J<0$ and $\det J>0$, and let $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2)$ with $d_1,d_2>0$. For any spatial eigenfunction of $-\Delta$ with eigenvalue $\lambda\ge0$, the linearized reaction-diffusion mode has matrix $J-\lambda D$. For the continuous rectangular torus, $\lambda=\lambda_k=\sum_j(2\pi k_j/L_j)^2$ with $k\in\mathbb Z^d$. For the periodic grid of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]], the mode indexed by $\ell$ has $\lambda=\lambda_{h,\ell}=4\sum_jh_j^{-2}\sin^2(\pi\ell_j/N_j)$, with $0\le\ell_j<N_j$.

Define
$$
\beta_T=d_2J_{11}+d_1J_{22},\qquad q(\lambda)=\det(J-\lambda D)=d_1d_2\lambda^2-\beta_T\lambda+\det J.
$$
For either domain or grid and each actual mode, $J-\lambda D$ has a positive-real-part eigenvalue exactly when $q(\lambda)<0$; it is Hurwitz exactly when $q(\lambda)>0$, and has a zero eigenvalue when $q(\lambda)=0$. Thus the continuous or discrete linear instability criterion tests the actual corresponding spectrum. If all nonnegative $\lambda$ are regarded as continuously available, then a diffusion-driven unstable band exists exactly when $\beta_T>0$ and $\beta_T^2>4d_1d_2\det J$; its endpoints are
$$
\lambda_\pm=\frac{\beta_T\pm\sqrt{\beta_T^2-4d_1d_2\det J}}{2d_1d_2}.
$$
On a bounded torus or a finite grid, the band criterion alone is not enough: at least one actual Laplacian eigenvalue must lie strictly between $\lambda_-$ and $\lambda_+$.

items.title: Finite-volume and periodic diffusion preserve intervals and weighted mass

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, updated author text, 2019
references.locator: Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3, PDF pp. 38–47: positive TPFA transmissibilities, conservative cell balances, and the diffusion energy form.

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §4, printed pp. 26–29: positivity of finite spatial diffusion discretizations; this item proves the mass-weighted interval result for the stated matrices.

items.statement: Consider either the no-flux TPFA cell system of [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]] or the periodic grid system of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]. Write its finite index set as $I$, its positive diagonal mass matrix as $M=\operatorname{diag}(m_i)$, and its stiffness matrix as $L$. In both cases $L=L^{\mathsf T}$, $L\mathbf1=0$, and $L_{ij}=-c_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$, where $c_{ij}=c_{ji}\ge0$. For each species $r$, let $d_r\ge0$ and solve $M u_r'+d_rLu_r=0$. Assume $a_r\le b_r$ for every species. If initially $u_{i,r}\in[a_r,b_r]$ for all $i,r$, then the solution exists for all $t\ge0$ and remains in those intervals. More precisely, each species evolution matrix has nonnegative entries and row sums one, so it is a contraction in the maximum norm. The flow also preserves each weighted species sum $\sum_i m_i u_{i,r}$ and therefore every finite linear combination of species sums, including $\mathcal M_{c,h}$ of [[def-stoichiometric-mass-invariant]].

items.title: Exact reaction-then-diffusion Lie step on FV or periodic grids

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §9, printed pp. 60–64: first-order operator splitting into separately solved diffusion and reaction subproblems.

items.statement:
**Input:** Either the no-flux TPFA discretization of [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]] or the periodic-grid discretization of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]; a reaction field $F$; a reaction-inward rectangle $R$ such that $F$ is $C^1$ on an open neighborhood of $R$ and $DF$ is bounded on some closed neighborhood of $R$; a state $U^n$ with each cell/node state in $R$; and a time step $\tau\ge0$.

**Procedure:**

1. At every cell/node $i$, solve the exact reaction IVP $\dot z=F(z)$ from $z(0)=U_i^n$ to time $\tau$, and set $V_i=\Phi_F^\tau(U_i^n)$.
2. For each species $r$, apply the exact diffusion map $e^{-\tau d_rM^{-1}L_h}$ in the TPFA case or $e^{-\tau d_rA_h^{\rm per}}$ in the periodic-grid case to the vector $(V_{i,r})_i$; call the output $U^{n+1}_{\cdot,r}$.
3. Return $U^{n+1}$.

This order is the **reaction-then-diffusion Lie composition**. The maps in both substeps are exact flows. The algorithm makes no claim about an approximate ODE or matrix-exponential solver; any such solver error requires a separate bound. Under the hypotheses of [[thm-quasipositive-reaction-flow-preserves-invariant-rectangle-and-mass]] and [[thm-fv-and-periodic-diffusion-flow-preserves-rectangles-and-mass]], each substep is well-defined for all finite $\tau$ on $R$.

items.title: Forward-Euler reaction followed by exact FV or periodic diffusion

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §6, printed pp. 39–40: forward-Euler reaction positivity under an explicit step restriction.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: §§1.3 and 2.2, PDF pp. 6–10: monotone finite-volume diffusion and nonnegative transmissibility conditions.

items.statement:
**Input:** Either the no-flux TPFA discretization of [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]] or the periodic-grid discretization of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]; a reaction field $F$; a reaction-inward rectangle $R$; coordinate constants $L_i\ge0$ such that $|F_i(z)-F_i(w)|\le L_i|z_i-w_i|$ whenever $z,w\in R$ differ only in coordinate $i$, as required in [[lem-forward-euler-reaction-step-preserves-invariant-rectangle-and-mass]]; $\tau_R=\min_{i:L_i>0}L_i^{-1}$, with $\tau_R=+\infty$ if every $L_i=0$; a state $U^n$ with every cell/node state in $R$; and $0\le\tau\le\tau_R$.

**Procedure:**

1. At every cell/node, compute the forward-Euler reaction value $V_i=U_i^n+\tau F(U_i^n)$.
2. For each species $r$, apply the exact diffusion map $e^{-\tau d_rM^{-1}L_h}$ in the TPFA case or $e^{-\tau d_rA_h^{\rm per}}$ in the periodic-grid case to $(V_{i,r})_i$.
3. Return the resulting state $U^{n+1}$.

This is an approximate reaction substep followed by exact diffusion. The bound $\tau\le\tau_R$ is part of the input contract and is needed for the stated rectangle guarantee; no diffusion CFL restriction is needed because the diffusion map is exact. The procedure makes no claim about finite-precision evaluation of either step.

items.title: Exact reaction-diffusion Lie steps preserve rectangles and mass balance

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §§4 and 9, printed pp. 26–27 and 60–64: reaction positivity and the reaction-then-diffusion Lie composition.

items.statement: Choose either the no-flux TPFA system of [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]] or the periodic grid system of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]], and use the exact reaction-then-diffusion step of [[alg-exact-lie-reaction-diffusion-step]]. Let $R=\prod_{r=1}^m[a_r,b_r]$ be reaction-inward, and suppose $F$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of $R$ with derivative bounded on a closed neighborhood. If every cell/node state of $U^n$ lies in $R$, then every cell/node state of $U^{n+1}$ lies in $R$ for every finite $\tau\ge0$. If $c^TF=0$ throughout $R$, then $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^{n+1})=\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^n)$; if $c^TF\le0$ throughout $R$, then $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^{n+1})\le\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^n)$. Here $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U)=\sum_i m_i c^TU_i$ uses the cell/node weights of the chosen discretization.

items.title: A bounded Euler-reaction Lie step preserves rectangles and mass balance

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §6, printed pp. 39–40: forward-Euler reaction positivity requires an explicit step bound.

items.statement: Choose either the no-flux TPFA system of [[def-fv-tpfa-no-flux-diffusion-specialization]] or the periodic grid system of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]]. Use [[alg-euler-reaction-lie-diffusion-step]] with a reaction-inward rectangle $R$, an initial state in $R$, and $0\le\tau\le\tau_R$ from [[lem-forward-euler-reaction-step-preserves-invariant-rectangle-and-mass]]. Then every component of the output state lies in $R$. The functional $\mathcal M_{c,h}$ is unchanged when $c^TF=0$ throughout $R$, and is nonincreasing when $c^TF\le0$ throughout $R$. The diffusion substep here is exact; no positivity assertion for a forward-Euler diffusion substep is made.

items.title: Mesh-uniform first-order Lie error for a smooth periodic reaction-diffusion solution

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §9, printed pp. 60–64: Lie splitting, its local commutator defect, and the need for bounds uniform in spatial discretization.

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.6–10.8, PDF pp. 149–153: smooth periodic reaction-diffusion modes and the vector model context.

items.statement:
Fix $T>0$, a rectangular torus $\mathbb T_L^d$, and $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)$ with $d_r\ge0$. Let $F\in C^2(U,\mathbb R^m)$ on an open neighborhood $U$ of a compact reaction-inward rectangle $R$, and let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^4(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R^m))$ solve $u_t=D\Delta u+F(u)$ with $u(x,t)\in R$. For each periodic grid of [[def-periodic-reaction-diffusion-grid]], let $P_hu(t)$ be the samples, and start the exact Lie algorithm [[alg-exact-lie-reaction-diffusion-step]] from $U^0=P_hu(0)$, using the periodic branch and uniform steps $\tau=T/N$. There is a constant $C_T$, depending on $u,F,D,R,T,L,d,m$ but not on the grid widths or $N$, such that
$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\|U^n-P_hu(t_n)\|_\infty\le C_T(\tau+h_{\max}^2),\qquad t_n=n\tau.
$$
The estimate is for exact reaction and diffusion subflows, a fixed smooth solution, and the periodic centered grid. It gives no error claim for a general finite-volume mesh, nonsmooth solutions, approximate subsolvers, or nonlinear cross-diffusion.

items.title: No-flux rectangular TPFA Lie error by even reflection

references.title: R. Eymard, T. Gallouët, and R. Herbin, Finite Volume Methods, updated author text, 2019
references.locator: Chapter 9 §§9.2–9.3, PDF pp. 38–47: orthogonal cell-centered fluxes and conservative boundary treatment.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^d(0,L_j)$ and let $u\in C^1([0,T];C^4(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^m))$ solve $u_t=D\Delta u+F(u)$ with $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_r)$, $d_r\ge0$, and range in a compact reaction-inward rectangle $R$. Assume $F\in C^2$ near $R$, homogeneous Neumann data hold, and the coordinatewise even reflection of $u$ across every face extends to a $C^1_tC^4_x$ function on the doubled torus $\prod_j(\mathbb R/2L_j\mathbb Z)$. On the uniform cell-centered grid of [[def-cell-centered-rectangular-no-flux-tpfa-grid]], start the exact reaction-then-diffusion Lie step of [[alg-exact-lie-reaction-diffusion-step]] from cell-center samples and use uniform $\tau=T/N$. Then a constant $C_T$, independent of the mesh widths and $N$, satisfies
$$
\max_{0\le n\le N}\|U^n-P_hu(t_n)\|_\infty\le C_T(\tau+h_{\max}^2),\qquad t_n=n\tau.
$$
This result is for rectangular Cartesian TPFA grids and solutions with the stated even $C^4$ boundary compatibility; it does not assert mesh-uniform accuracy for general admissible polyhedral meshes.

title: Reaction-diffusion systems, invariants and pattern computation — Examples

items.title: Consistent-mass P1 diffusion can leave the nonnegative cone
items.statement:
On the interval $[0,2h]$ with three uniform P1 nodes and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, the semidiscrete heat equation with consistent mass matrix,
$$
M\dot u+\nu Ku=0,\qquad \nu>0,
$$
does not preserve nodal nonnegativity: there is a nonnegative initial vector for which the first component becomes negative immediately.

items.title: A Brusselator with a continuous Turing-unstable torus mode

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §§10.6–10.7, PDF pp. 149–151: general reaction-diffusion systems and linear Turing mode analysis. The explicit Brusselator field and its calculations are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Consider the Brusselator field
$$
F(u,v)=\bigl(1-\tfrac52u+u^2v,\ \tfrac32u-u^2v\bigr)
$$
with diagonal diffusivity $D=\operatorname{diag}(1/10,2)$. Its homogeneous equilibrium is $(u_*,v_*)=(1,3/2)$. On the one-dimensional torus of length $L=4\pi/3$, the continuous reaction-diffusion linearization has an unstable Fourier mode with wave number $k=1$.

items.title: A three-cell periodic grid suppresses the Brusselator's unstable continuous mode

references.title: Luca Doria, Numerical Algorithms, lecture notes, Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz, 2022
references.locator: §10.7, PDF pp. 150–151: general diffusion-dependent mode matrices. The Brusselator and the three-cell spectral calculation are supplied locally.

items.title: A forward-Euler Fisher–KPP reaction step preserves its interval under a sharp simple bound

references.title: Willem Hundsdorfer, Numerical Solution of Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Equations, lecture notes for Ph.D. course, 1996
references.locator: §6, printed pp. 39–40: forward-Euler positivity bounds for reaction updates; the scalar interval calculation is verified here.

items.statement: Let $r>0$ and use the scalar Fisher–KPP reaction $F(u)=ru(1-u)$ on $R=[0,1]$, followed by exact no-flux TPFA diffusion with any diffusivity $d\ge0$. For a nonnegative step $\tau$, the forward-Euler reaction map preserves $[0,1]$ for every starting value $u\in[0,1]$ exactly when $0\le\tau r\le1$; after that step, exact no-flux TPFA diffusion also preserves the interval. For $\tau>0$, on any finite grid with positive cell weights, the reaction strictly increases the discrete mass if at least one cell value lies in $(0,1)$ and leaves it unchanged if every cell value is a reaction equilibrium $0$ or $1$. At $\tau=0$ the reaction map is the identity. This example makes no mass-conservation claim.
